citation: Tests/MusterCoreTests/CompositionArbiterTests.swift, and the bug that prompted the type
why: Exactly one thing may reach the pane per key press. This type exists because of a bug that reached a user: every printable key arrived twice, because AppKit's insertText sent the committed text and the key encoder sent the keystroke, and nothing decided between them. Typing `hello` produced `hheelllloo`. The property worth pinning is not any single case below - it is that there is one outcome per press, always.

cases.name: plain key is not also its text
cases.why: The regression itself. AppKit calls insertText("h") for a plain `h` with no input method involved, so a committed string is present here - and it must still lose to the keystroke, or every printable character is sent twice.

cases.name: a finished composition is its text, not the key that finished it
cases.why: option+e then e: the second press ends the composition and produces `é`, which has no relationship to the `e` that was pressed. Sending the keystroke here would put a bare `e` in the pane.

cases.name: a press that opens a composition reaches nothing
cases.why: option+e alone: a preedit opens and the pane must not see the keystroke sitting behind it. The input method owns the key until it commits.

cases.name: a commit that re-marks in the same press reaches nothing
cases.why: Candidate selection in a CJK input method commits text and opens a new preedit in one press. Still the method's business, so the pane sees nothing - the committed text will arrive with whatever eventually ends the composition.

cases.name: an empty commit falls back to the keystroke
cases.why: Escaping out of a preedit ends the composition without producing text. Treating that as sendText("") would silently eat the key, so escape would appear to do nothing at all.

cases.name: a composition that commits nothing at all falls back to the keystroke
cases.why: Same as the empty commit, reached by the other route: the method ends the composition without calling insertText. Both spellings of `produced no text` have to behave alike, or the outcome depends on which method the user has installed.
